title: Refactor Without Changing Behaviour
description: Improve structure, naming, and readability while guaranteeing the observable behaviour stays identical.
template:
Refactor this code to be clearer and easier to change, **without changing its observable behaviour**.

Language / framework: [E.G. C# / ASP.NET CORE]

The smell that bothers me: [E.G. LONG METHOD, DEEP NESTING, DUPLICATION, POOR NAMES]

Code:
---
[PASTE CODE HERE]
---

Please:
1. Do refactoring in **safe, behaviour-preserving steps**, not one giant rewrite.
2. Keep the public API the same unless you explain why it must change.
3. Improve names, remove duplication, and reduce nesting.
4. Note any **behavioural risks** in the current code (hidden bugs, edge cases) separately — do not silently fix them.
5. Show the refactored version and a short list of the specific changes and their rationale.

Do not add new features, new dependencies, or speculative abstractions.

Code: the CreateOrder action.

1. Do refactoring in safe, behaviour-preserving steps.
2. Keep the public API the same.

tips: Name the specific smell so the output targets what actually bothers you
Keep the 'note risks separately, do not fix them' rule — it prevents a refactor turning into an unrequested behaviour change
Run your tests after each step rather than after the whole rewrite
